name: C string utilities
description: A C utility library with buffer overflows (strcpy, gets), a format-string vulnerability, command injection via system(), MD5 password hashing, an integer-overflow in malloc and hard-coded credentials. Intentionally insecure, for education.
expected: Findings from the C/C++ token scanner.

fixes.title: Load credentials from environment variables
fixes.explanation: Credentials are no longer in the source binary.

fixes.title: Replace strcpy and gets with safe alternatives
fixes.explanation: snprintf and fgets require an explicit length.

fixes.title: Use a literal format string
fixes.explanation: printf receives "%s" as a literal format; the message is the argument.

fixes.title: Use execv instead of system
fixes.explanation: No shell expands the argument; dir is a single token to /bin/ls.

fixes.title: Use calloc to avoid integer-overflow in size calculation
fixes.explanation: calloc(count, size) multiplies safely and zero-initialises; malloc(n * size) can overflow silently.

fixes.title: Use SHA-256 instead of MD5
fixes.explanation: SHA-256 is not broken. Use a password-hashing function (libsodium argon2) for password storage.
